commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Align with AB3 template and v1.4
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide has no Acknowledgements section, and most of its
implementation notes have no design considerations. Its use cases do
not follow the AB3 format, some requirements are inaccurate, and its
manual tests repeat the same index checks for every command.

The tP requires an accurate Acknowledgements section, and evaluators
compare the DG against the AB3 template and the latest release.

Let's update the DG, keeping the v1.4 content that is already there:

* Restore the Acknowledgements section
* Add implementation sections, with design considerations, for nested
  indexes, gig editing, safe deletion, cross-client views, and the
  summary
* Restore the proposed undo/redo design and add a proposed data
  archiving design
* Rewrite the user stories, use cases, NFRs, and glossary in the AB3
  format, and label unimplemented user stories as planned
* Lower the capacity NFR to 1000 gigs and payment obligations, as the
  app has not been tested with 5000
* Add manual tests for summary, and test index validation only once
* Add an Effort appendix
Developer Guide: Align with AB3 template and v1.4

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor code to follow Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle passes, but it does not check some parts of the Java
coding standard (intermediate). Several booleans do not read as
true/false statements, the same invalid gig and payment index
messages are defined in up to 8 commands, and a few methods mix
several steps. Many tests also check several groups of inputs without
saying which group each case belongs to, which makes them harder to
review and grade.

Let's align the code with the standard, without changing behavior:

* Rename booleans to read as statements, e.g. CommandResult's
  shouldShowHelp() and shouldExit(), and PaymentObligation's isPaid.
  The saved JSON key "paid" is unchanged.
* Move MESSAGE_INVALID_GIG_INDEX and MESSAGE_INVALID_PAYMENT_INDEX
  into Messages
* Split SummaryCommand#execute, MainWindow#executeCommand, and
  GigabyteData#matchReplacementGigIndexes into named steps
* Wrap lines close to the 120-character limit
* Make @TempDir fields package-private
* Label equivalence partitions and boundary values in tests, and split
  mixed invalid-input tests into one test per input group

The public value fields inherited from AB3, such as Name#fullName and
Phone#value, are kept as an accepted template exception.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag: Limit tag names to 25 characters
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag names accept any number of alphanumeric characters. A very long
tag, such as one over 1000 characters, cannot be viewed properly in
the client list.

Let's reject tags longer than 25 characters in add and edit, and
document the limit in the User Guide.

The limit is not applied when loading the data file. A stricter load
check would make an older file with a long tag invalid, so Gigabyte
would start with an empty client list and overwrite the file on the
next save.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Phone numbers accept digits only. Common formats such as
+65 9123 4567 and 6123-4567 are rejected, which is a problem for users
with overseas clients and counts as overzealous validation.

Let's accept an optional leading '+', followed by groups of digits
joined by a single space or hyphen, with at least 3 digits in total.
Numbers are stored as typed. Every existing digits-only number is
still valid, so older data files keep loading.

Let's also update the error message and the UG, and regroup PhoneTest
by equivalence partition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Reject quoted cents and paid values
commitResults.messageBody:
The current-format reader rejects floating-point cents, but Jackson
still converts quoted numbers and booleans. A save file with
"feeCents": "125050" or "paid": "true" loads, and the next save
silently rewrites it.

Let's read feeCents, amountCents and paid through deserializers that
accept only a JSON integer or a JSON boolean. Jackson 2.7 has no
setting to turn off this conversion. The deserializers apply only to
these adapters, so the shared mapper and the preferences reader are
unchanged.

commitResults.messageBody:

GigabyteParser matches command words exactly, so LIST, List and AddGig
are rejected as unknown commands. The PE guidance treats keywords that
are case-sensitive for no reason as a feature flaw.

Let's lower-case the command word with Locale.ROOT before matching it.
All COMMAND_WORD constants are already lower case. Arguments are left
as typed, so names, titles and keywords keep their case.

Let's also note in the UG command-format notes that command words are
not case-sensitive.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate clients ignoring case and spacing
commitResults.messageBody:
Client names are compared exactly, so add and edit accept John Doe,
john doe and John  Doe as three different clients. The PE guidance
treats exact-match-only duplicate detection as a feature flaw.

Let's compare names after ignoring case, leading and trailing spaces,
and repeated internal spaces, but only in the add and edit commands.

* add rejects a name matching another client's normalised name.
* edit rejects such a name only when the edit changes the client's
  normalised name, leaving the edited client out by UID. Case-only
  and spacing-only fixes stay allowed, and the exact-name check
  still applies.
* add and edit save, but add a note, when another client has the
  same phone number or email (email compared ignoring case).

The load-time check and Client#isSameClient stay exact. A stricter
load rule would reject older files holding John Doe and john doe,
start the app with empty data, and let the next command overwrite
the file. Such files still load, and both clients stay editable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show index error for invalid index values
commitResults.messageBody:
Every parser that takes an index catches the error from
ParserUtil#parseIndex and rethrows it as 'Invalid command format'. So
`delete 0` reports a format error, even though the format is correct
and only the value is wrong.

Let's add ParserUtil#parseIndexes, which checks the number of indexes
before parsing each one, and use it in all 11 parsers that take indexes.

* A missing or extra index, or extra words before the first prefix,
  still shows the invalid command format message with the usage.
* An index that is zero, negative or not an integer now shows 'Index
  must be a positive integer.'

Let's also update the parser tests, the UG section on indexes and the
DG manual tests to quote the new messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: findgig: Ignore punctuation around title words
commitResults.messageBody:
findgig splits a gig title on whitespace and compares each word with
the keywords. A title such as 'Invoice, overdue' yields the word
'Invoice,', so 'findgig invoice' reports that no gigs match.

Let's ignore Unicode punctuation at the start or end of each word when
comparing.

* Keep punctuation inside a word, so 'commerce' still does not match
  'e-commerce'.
* Keep symbols and accent marks, so 'c' does not match 'C++' and '100'
  does not match '$100'.
* Require an exact match for a keyword made only of punctuation, so
  'findgig -' does not match every title.

Angle brackets are math symbols in Unicode, so '<draft>' does not match
'draft'. Such titles seem rare enough to accept this.

commitResults.messageTitle: LogicManagerTest: Check formatted phones survive saving
commitResults.messageBody:
PhoneTest and ParserUtilTest check formatted phone numbers such as
+65 9123 4567 on their own, but no test runs one through a full

Let's add a test that adds a client with +65 9123 4567, edits it to
+1-202-555-0143, and reloads the data file after each step to check
the number is kept as typed.

The clear command replies "Address book has been cleared!", which is
left over from AddressBook-Level3. Gigabyte has no address book, and
the message does not say that gigs and payment obligations are deleted
too, which matters for a destructive command.

payment obligations." The Developer Guide's manual test for clear is
updated to expect the new message.

commitResults.messageTitle: SampleDataUtil: Use client tags in sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
The sample clients are tagged friends, colleagues, neighbours, family
and classmates. These are left over from AddressBook-Level3 and make
Gigabyte look like a personal contacts list rather than a client
manager. The add command's usage message and the User Guide examples
use similar personal tags.

Let's,

  and startup
* use client tags in the add usage message and User Guide examples
* replace the Newgate Prison address in the User Guide add example

The deadlines command ignores any input after the command word, so
'deadlines unexpected' shows the overview instead of an error. This is
inconsistent with outstanding, which rejects extra input.

Let's reject extra input for deadlines the same way.

* Add a MESSAGE_USAGE to DeadlinesCommand
* Extract the existing outstanding check into
  GigabyteParser#requireNoArguments and use it for both commands
* Update the UG and DG to list which no-parameter commands ignore
  extra input and which reject it

summary, help, list, exit and clear still ignore extra input.

commitResults.messageTitle: GigTitle: Reject titles of only non-breaking spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
GigTitle trims titles with String#strip(), which keeps Unicode spaces
such as the non-breaking space (U+00A0). A title made only of them
passes validation, and the gig is shown with a blank title.

Let's trim both the whitespace String#strip() removes and Unicode
whitespace (the White_Space property). Such titles are then rejected
with the usual title error, and Unicode spaces around a valid title
are removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply coding standard to parsers, model and UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Some classes break the se-edu Java coding standard or the textbook's
code quality guidelines: magic numbers, a nested ternary, fully
qualified names instead of imports, an unused logger, fields that are
never reassigned but not final, and related constants without a
common prefix.

Let's fix these without changing what the app does:

* Name the expected index count in the payment parsers and build the
  invalid-format message in one place
* Replace the nested ternary in PaymentObligationListPanel with if
  statements, and prefix its related constants
* Name the cell width padding in GigListPanel
* Remove the unused logger in ClientListPanel
* Make storage fields final and use Optional#isEmpty
* Include payment obligations in GigabyteData#hashCode, matching
  equals

commitResults.messageTitle: Share model setup across command tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Six command tests copy the same createModel() helper, and three of
them also copy the same addGig() helper. A change to the shared setup
has to be repeated in every copy.

Let's move both helpers into a TypicalModels test utility. The call
sites stay the same through static imports.
